scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
question: What is Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students (PMS-SC)?
answer: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students is a SC scheme of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice & Empowerment), implemented at the central level in All India (all States/UTs). Type: Centrally Sponsored Scheme. Launched: 1944 (pre-independence scheme, revised many times). Status: Active. It aims to help Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10 (Class 11 to PhD, including professional, technical and vocational courses). Benefit: Reimbursement of all compulsory non-refundable fees (tuition, admission, exam, etc.) charged by the institution plus a monthly maintenance allowance. Also covers study tour charges (up to Rs 1,600 p.a.), thesis typing/printing (up to Rs 1,600 for PhD), book grant, and coaching for competitive exams for courses of less than one year; paid by DBT into Aadhaar-linked bank account

scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
question: Who is eligible for Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students?
answer: Target group: Scheduled Caste students studying after Class 10 (Class 11 to PhD, including professional, technical and vocational courses). Beneficiary type: Student. Age: No specific age limit. Income limit: Family annual income up to Rs 2,50,000 from all sources. Other conditions: Student must belong to a Scheduled Caste; must be enrolled in a recognised post-matriculation course (Class 11/12, ITI, polytechnic, diploma, UG, PG, professional degree) in a government-recognised institution in India; scholarship is payable only for the prescribed duration of the course; student must not hold any other centrally funded scholarship for the same period Not eligible: Students who fail to promote to the next class lose the scholarship; only two members of a family can get this (and other such) scholarships simultaneously; distance/correspondence courses allowed only if the institution is recognised and there is no regular course available; income certificate and caste certificate from competent authority are mandatory

scheme_name: Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students
question: What benefits/amount does Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Caste Students give?
answer: Reimbursement of all compulsory non-refundable fees (tuition, admission, exam, etc.) charged by the institution plus a monthly maintenance allowance. Full compulsory fees paid Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored - 60:40 Centre:State for most States; 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States (100% central for UTs without legislature).

answer: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students is a ST scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs, implemented at the central level in All India. Type: Central Sector Schemes (Fellowship + Scholarship components). Launched: Fellowship component running since 2000s with new design from 2019-20; Top Class Scholarship from 2013-14. Status: Active. It aims to help Meritorious ST students pursuing higher education in premier institutes (Top Class) and MPhil/PhD (Fellowship). Benefit: Monthly fellowship for research scholars and, under the Top Class component, tuition and living allowance for ST students in premier institutions

scheme_name: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students
question: Who is eligible for National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students?
answer: Target group: Meritorious ST students pursuing higher education in premier institutes (Top Class) and MPhil/PhD (Fellowship). Beneficiary type: Student; Researcher. Age: As per institute norms for the course. Income limit: Fellowship - no income ceiling; Top Class Scholarship - family income up to Rs 6 lakh per annum. Other conditions: Fellowship: 750 fresh ST scholars per year selected on merit in the Master's degree for MPhil/PhD, with preference to girls, divyangjan and PVTG candidates. Top Class: admission to prescribed courses in about 252-265 identified premier institutes (IITs, IIMs, AIIMS, NITs etc.) Not eligible: Candidates receiving another fellowship/salary cannot hold this fellowship; award requires submission of progress reports

scheme_name: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students
question: What benefits/amount does National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of Scheduled Tribe Students give?
answer: Monthly fellowship for research scholars and, under the Top Class component, tuition and living allowance for ST students in premier institutions Headline value: Fellowship: MPhil Rs 25,000 per month and PhD Rs 28,000 per month (as per latest rates) plus contingency; 750 fresh fellowships per year. Top Class: full tuition, living expenses, book grant and computer allowance, income ceiling Rs 6 lakh Funding pattern: 100% Central (Central Sector Schemes).

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan
question: What is Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN)?
answer: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan is a PVTG scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs (coordinating 9 Central Ministries), implemented at the central level in All India (PVTG habitations in 18 States/UTs). Type: Central Sector/Centrally Sponsored mission (multi-ministry convergence). Launched: 15 November 2023 (Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, from Khunti, Jharkhand). Status: Active. It aims to help Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) - 75 PVTGs across the country. Benefit: Saturation of PVTG habitations with pucca houses, roads, mobile connectivity, electricity, solar power, drinking water, community water supply, education (hostels, anganwadis), health facilities, and skill/livelihood support

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan
question: Who is eligible for Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan?
answer: Target group: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) - 75 PVTGs across the country. Beneficiary type: Family; Village; Community. Age: Not applicable. Income limit: No separate income ceiling; eligibility is PVTG habitation/residence. Other conditions: PVTG households in habitations identified by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (about 4.9 lakh households); benefits delivered through 11 critical interventions Not eligible: Non-PVTG households in the same village may be covered only for common infrastructure, per guidelines

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan
question: What benefits/amount does Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan give?
answer: Saturation of PVTG habitations with pucca houses, roads, mobile connectivity, electricity, solar power, drinking water, community water supply, education (hostels, anganwadis), health facilities, and skill/livelihood support Headline value: Total outlay Rs 24,104 crore (Centre Rs 15,336 crore + States Rs 8,768 crore) - the largest ever scheme for PVTGs. About 4.9 lakh pucca houses at about Rs 2.39 lakh per house; 500 hostels at about Rs 2.75 crore each; 2,500 anganwadi centres; 3,000 mobile towers; 8,000 km of roads; multi-purpose centres; 1,000 mobile medical units and solar power to 1.5 lakh households Funding pattern: Centrally Sponsored with State share; convergence with existing ministries' budgets (DAPST).

scheme_name: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan
question: What is Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA)?
answer: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan is a ST scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs (nodal; 17 line ministries implementing), implemented at the central level in All India (tribal-majority villages in 30 States/UTs). Type: Mission with convergence funding (Development Action Plan for Scheduled Tribes - DAPST). Launched: 2 October 2024 (launched from Hazaribagh, Jharkhand). Status: Active. It aims to help Tribal-majority villages and aspirational blocks - about 5 crore tribal people. Benefit: Saturation of critical gaps in social infrastructure, health, education, livelihood and connectivity through 25 interventions, including all-weather roads, mobile connectivity, tribal hostels, multipurpose marketing centres, tourist home-stays, FRA patta holder support, sickle-cell disease centres of competence and mobile medical units

Income limit: Not applicable (village-based saturation approach). Other conditions: Villages with more than 50% ST population and population above 500, plus aspirational blocks; 63,843 villages in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks across 30 States/UTs Not eligible: Not an individual application scheme - interventions are planned village-wise by States/line ministries

scheme_name: Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP)
question: What is Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP) (PMJVM)?
answer: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP) is a ST scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs (implemented through TRIFED), implemented at the central level in All India. Type: Central Sector Scheme (100% central funding). Launched: PMVDY launched 14 April 2018; MSP for MFP operational from 2013-14; both consolidated into PMJVM from 2021-22. Status: Active. It aims to help Tribal gatherers of minor forest produce (MFP), tribal artisans, tribal entrepreneurs and SHGs. Benefit: MSP-backed procurement of minor forest produce, value addition and market linkage for tribal products, e-commerce/retail support (Tribes India) and micro-enterprise training for tribal SHG clusters

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP)
question: Who is eligible for Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (Van Dhan + MSP for MFP)?

Income limit: No income ceiling; intended for tribal MFP gatherers and artisans. Other conditions: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras (VDVK) are formed as clusters of 15 tribal SHGs with about 300 members each; Value Chain Development Centres process and market MFP; MSP procurement through State agencies Not eligible: Non-tribal producers are not eligible for MFP MSP support; benefits flow through SHG clusters

scheme_name: NSTFDC schemes - Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, term loans and Adivasi Shiksha Rinn Yojana
question: What is NSTFDC schemes - Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, term loans and Adivasi Shiksha Rinn Yojana (NSTFDC)?
answer: NSTFDC schemes - Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, term loans and Adivasi Shiksha Rinn Yojana is a ST scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs, implemented at the central level in All India (through State Channelizing Agencies). Launched: NSTFDC incorporated 2001 (under the Companies Act; earlier operations from 1993 as a division). Status: Active. Benefit: Concessional term loans (up to 90% of unit cost) for income generation, with an exclusive women's window (AMSY) and education loans for ST students

scheme_name: NSTFDC schemes - Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana, term loans and Adivasi Shiksha Rinn Yojana

question: What is Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs (VTC in Tribal Areas)?

scheme_name: Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs

Other conditions: ST youth enrolled in short-term vocational courses in trades with market demand; training institutions receive central grants per trainee Not eligible: Non-tribal youth; courses without placement/market linkage are discouraged

scheme_name: Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs
question: What benefits/amount does Vocational Training Centres in Tribal Areas / Skill Development for STs give?

scheme_name: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme
question: What is Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme (FRA / Forest Rights Act)?
answer: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme is a ST scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs (policy) with Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and States, implemented at the central level in All India. Type: Statutory framework with central support for implementation. Launched: Act passed 2006; came into force 31 December 2007; rules amended 2012. Status: Active. It aims to help Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. Benefit: Legal recognition of individual and community forest rights including land titles (pattas), rights over minor forest produce, community forest resource management and rehabilitation in case of displacement

scheme_name: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme
question: Who is eligible for Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme?
answer: Target group: Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. Beneficiary type: Individual; Family; Community. Age: Not applicable. Income limit: No income ceiling. Other conditions: Forest dwellers who have lived in forests for at least three generations (75 years) and depend on forests for livelihood; individual rights (homestead, cultivation) and community rights (community forest resource, grazing, minor forest produce, conversion of pattas) Not eligible: Claims must be supported by evidence and recommended by the Gram Sabha and Forest Rights Committee; unsupported claims rejected

scheme_name: Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme
question: What benefits/amount does Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act - implementation programme give?
answer: Legal recognition of individual and community forest rights including land titles (pattas), rights over minor forest produce, community forest resource management and rehabilitation in case of displacement Headline value: Rights-based (no cash grant). About 24-25 lakh individual titles and over 1 lakh community titles recognised since 2008; title holders can access DAJGUA support for agriculture, animal husbandry and fishery under FRA pattas Funding pattern: Central support for implementation and digitisation; State Governments execute the process.

Helpline: State Tribal Development Department / District FRA cell.

scheme_name: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub
question: What is National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub (NSSH / SC-ST Hub)?
answer: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub is a SC & ST scheme of Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, implemented at the central level in All India. Type: Central Sector Scheme. Launched: 2016 (launched by the Prime Minister in October 2016; extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26). Status: Active. It aims to help SC/ST owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and SC/ST entrepreneurs. Benefit: Capacity building and training, Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy (SCLCSS), procurement support to meet the 4% government procurement mandate, GeM and Single Point Registration assistance, reimbursement of bank loan processing fees, exhibition/marketing support and mentorship

scheme_name: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub
question: Who is eligible for National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub?
answer: Target group: SC/ST owned micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and SC/ST entrepreneurs. Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur; MSME. Age: 18 years and above. Income limit: No income ceiling (enterprise-based scheme). Other conditions: MSME with Udyam Registration (or willing to register) having at least 51% SC/ST ownership; manufacturing, service, trading or agri-allied enterprise for most components; for SCLCSS - SC/ST ownership above 51% with institutional loan for new plant and machinery Not eligible: Non-SC/ST majority enterprises; second-hand machinery (for capital subsidy); dual benefit from a similar subsidy is not allowed

scheme_name: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub
question: What benefits/amount does National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub give?
answer: Capacity building and training, Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy (SCLCSS), procurement support to meet the 4% government procurement mandate, GeM and Single Point Registration assistance, reimbursement of bank loan processing fees, exhibition/marketing support and mentorship Headline value: Capital subsidy of 25% on institutional loan for plant and machinery, capped at Rs 25 lakh (SCLCSS); up to 90% of course fee capped at Rs 1 lakh for training reimbursements; up to 80% of pledge/bank-guarantee charges capped at Rs 1 lakh for tender participation; 100% subsidy on NSIC Single Point Registration Scheme fees Funding pattern: 100% Central (outlay about Rs 588 crore for 2021-22 to 2025-26).

scheme_name: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub
question: How do I apply for National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub?
answer: Application mode: Online registration on the SC-ST Hub portal; SCLCSS applications routed offline through the prime lending institution (bank) to SIDBI/NABARD. Portal: https://www.scsthub.in. Documents needed: Udyam Registration certificate; SC/ST caste certificate of proprietor/directors; ownership proof showing 51%+ SC/ST shareholding; PAN; GST; project report; machinery quotations/invoices for SCLCSS; loan sanction letter; bank account. Helpline: SC-ST Hub helpline (Ministry of MSME); offices in major cities including Delhi.

scheme_name: National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub
question: What are the latest changes in National Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Hub?

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme
question: What is Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (SCLCSS)?
answer: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme is a SC & ST scheme of Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (sub-scheme under National SC-ST Hub), implemented at the central level in All India. Type: Central Sector Scheme (sub-scheme of NSSH). Launched: 2016 (sub-scheme of the National SC-ST Hub). Status: Active. It aims to help SC/ST owned micro and small enterprises (manufacturing and services). Benefit: Capital subsidy to reduce the cost of new plant and machinery financed by a bank/institution, improving the viability of SC/ST manufacturing and service units

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme
question: Who is eligible for Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme?
answer: Target group: SC/ST owned micro and small enterprises (manufacturing and services). Beneficiary type: MSME; Entrepreneur. Age: 18 years and above (proprietor/directors). Income limit: No income ceiling. Other conditions: Micro or small enterprise with valid Udyam Registration and at least 51% SC/ST ownership; institutional term loan sanctioned for purchase of new plant and machinery/equipment; no sector-specific restriction; SC/ST units upgraded to medium within 3 years remain eligible Not eligible: Second-hand machinery; enterprises without institutional finance; applicants who already got a similar capital subsidy (no dual benefit)

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme
question: What benefits/amount does Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme give?
answer: Capital subsidy to reduce the cost of new plant and machinery financed by a bank/institution, improving the viability of SC/ST manufacturing and service units Headline value: 25% capital subsidy on the institutional loan amount, capped at Rs 25,00,000 per enterprise (eligible term loan typically up to Rs 1 crore) Funding pattern: 100% Central; disbursed through SIDBI/NABARD to the lending bank account of the beneficiary.

scheme_name: Special Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme

Helpline: SC-ST Hub helpline; MSME Development Institutes (MSME-DIs).

scheme_name: Stand-Up India Scheme
question: What is Stand-Up India Scheme (SUI)?
answer: Stand-Up India Scheme is a SC & ST scheme of Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, implemented at the central level in All India. Type: Central Sector Scheme (credit guarantee backed). Launched: 5 April 2016. Status: Active. It aims to help SC, ST and women entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises. Benefit: Composite bank loan (term loan plus working capital) for new enterprises, with collateral-free credit up to Rs 1 crore covered under the Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Stand-Up India Loans, plus Rupay debit card and handholding support through the Standup Mitra portal

scheme_name: Stand-Up India Scheme
question: Who is eligible for Stand-Up India Scheme?
answer: Target group: SC, ST and women entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises. Beneficiary type: Entrepreneur. Age: 18 years and above. Income limit: No income ceiling. Other conditions: SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneur; greenfield project (first venture of the beneficiary in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activity); for non-individual entities at least 51% shareholding and controlling stake must be with SC/ST and/or woman entrepreneurs; borrower must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution Not eligible: Expansion of existing business; retail trading restricted in certain years; persons with existing bank defaults

scheme_name: Stand-Up India Scheme
